sources.note: Nothing. Rationale (p. 2): 'There is no evidence that the language exists'; cites Glottolog 'unattested', Lobel 2013 ('no linguistic data exists..') and Reid 1987 ('no source of data for this language').

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: Issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. Sec. 3.2.23 'Tayabas "Ayta"', p. 93; also p. 56 and p. 240 fn. 10.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. States that the group 'exists in name but does not natively speak any language except Tagalog', that 'no linguistic data exists for any language that the ancestors of this group might have once spoken', and that there is no evidence they ever had a language distinct from any other Philippine language (p. 93).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record taya1256 (classification Unattested > Austronesian (Unattested); iso_retirement reason 'non-existent'; Glottolog's most extensive description = Reid 1994 and Garvan 1964, both a wordlist or less).

sources.note: Nothing; confirms no descriptive source exists (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).

sources.citation: Reid, Lawrence A. 1994. Possible non-Austronesian lexical elements in Philippine Negrito languages. Oceanic Linguistics 33(1): 37-74 (author's revised preprint on ScholarSpace).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing about Tayabas Ayta: the word 'Tayabas' does not occur; all 'Ayta' wordlists (sec. 2.2.7 and the wordlist inventory, p. 31 of preprint) are Zambales/Bataan/Pampanga Ayta. Only stress remark is a general transcription note ('Where stress has been indicated, it is marked as an acute accent'). Glottolog's listing of this as the Glottolog's most extensive description (a wordlist or less, 1 p.) is empty for this variety.

sources.citation: Reid, Lawrence A. 1987. The Early Switch Hypothesis: Linguistic evidence for contact between Negritos and Austronesians. Man and Culture in Oceania 3 (Special Issue): 41-59.
